name: PAD walking program
pitch: A progressive walking plan to manage claudication symptoms from peripheral artery disease.
instructions:
Design a progressive walking program for peripheral artery disease with claudication management.

Start by searching the web for reputable medical sources on PAD walking therapy, focusing on guidelines for claudication management. Look for programs that balance walking distance with rest intervals to improve pain-free walking time.

When the search results are gathered, review the key recommendations: typical starting distances, recommended rest periods when pain reaches a moderate level, and weekly progression targets. If the search returns no clear guidelines, say so and ask the person whether they want a generic plan or to consult their doctor for a personalised prescription.

Create a simple text page using make_page that outlines the program structure: a typical session format (walk until moderate pain, rest until pain subsides, repeat), a weekly progression schedule (e.g., increase walking time by 5 minutes every 2 weeks), and safety notes (stop and seek help if pain is severe, watch for skin changes).

If the person wants a routine, use routine_create to set a weekly reminder to log walking distance and pain levels each day. When nothing is found during the search, say plainly what could not be checked and offer to create a basic placeholder plan instead.

At the end, show the person the text page with the program details and ask if they want it saved, turned into a routine, or adjusted.

skills.name: research-pad-walking-guidelines
skills.description: Find evidence-based walking therapy for claudication
skills.body:
1. Use web_search to find guidelines from medical organisations on PAD and claudication.
2. Scan results for recommended walking duration, rest intervals, and progression rates.
3. Note the typical starting point: e.g., walk until moderate pain, rest until pain subsides, repeat 5–10 times.
4. If results are unclear or conflicting, say so and ask the person whether they want a generic plan or a doctor's advice.
5. Summarise the key numbers found (e.g., 'most plans start with 30 minutes total, including rest').

skills.name: build-the-walking-plan-page
skills.description: Make a text page with the program structure
skills.body:
1. Use make_page to create a page titled 'Progressive Walking Plan for PAD'.
2. Include a session format: 'Walk until pain reaches moderate level (3–4/10). Rest until pain drops to 1–2/10 or disappears. Repeat 3–5 times.'
3. Add a weekly progression: 'Increase total walking time by 5 minutes every 2 weeks, keeping the rest‑until‑pain‑subsides pattern.'
4. List safety notes: stop if pain is severe or sudden, check feet daily for sores, and consult a doctor before changing the plan.
5. Show the page to the person and ask if they want it saved or turned into a routine.

readme:
# PAD Walking Program
A progressive walking plan to manage claudication symptoms from peripheral artery disease.

What it does: searches for walking guidelines, creates a text page with a session format and weekly progression, and can set a reminder to log walks.

What it needs: web_search to find guidelines, make_page to output the plan, routine_create for optional reminders.

What it will not do: give a diagnosis or replace a doctor's advice; it always presents the plan as a general template and asks the person to check with their clinician.
